word:hebrew:H1148.explanation: Beninu is a Hebrew personal name used to identify one individual in Nehemiah 10:13. It does not function as an ordinary descriptive word in the available record, and its precise significance cannot be determined from the name alone. The occurrence preserves it as a name rather than translating it into a common English meaning. Thus, readers should understand Beninu primarily as the person’s identifying name, while the surrounding verse supplies any further contextual role. This name appears once in the Old Testament corpus.

word:hebrew:H118.explanation: Adalia is a Hebrew personal name, preserved as “Adalia” rather than translated into an ordinary descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Esther 9:8, and identifies a person in the biblical record. Because no lexical definition is provided beyond the name itself, its safest meaning is the personal designation “Adalia,” not an inferred character trait or spiritual idea.

word:hebrew:H1184.explanation: Baale-Jehudah is a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H1207.explanation: Bitstsah means a swamp, fen, or mire.

word:hebrew:H1272.explanation: Barach means to bolt or flee suddenly.

word:hebrew:H1351.explanation: Gaal means to soil or desecrate—to defile or pollute.

word:hebrew:H143.explanation: Adar means the twelfth Hebrew month.

word:hebrew:H1434.explanation: Gedil means a thread or tassel, including a fringe. It can also refer to a wreath or festoon.

word:hebrew:H1526.explanation: Gilonite means an inhabitant of Giloh.

word:hebrew:H1580.explanation: Gamal means to treat someone, whether by doing good or repaying what is due. It can also mean to wean a child.

word:hebrew:H1791.explanation: Dêk means this. It can also mean same, referring back to the same person or thing.

word:hebrew:H1827.explanation: Demamah means quiet or silence. It can also describe calm.

word:hebrew:H1852.explanation: Doq means something fine or thin, like a curtain.

word:hebrew:H1885.explanation: Dathan is the name of an Israelite, one of the sons of Eliab.

word:hebrew:H1931.explanation: Hûwʼ means he, she, or it. It can also point to someone or something as this or that.

word:hebrew:H2071.explanation: Zabud is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an ordinary action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Kings 4:5, and is rendered “Zabud.” Because this word functions as a name, its meaning for readers is chiefly identification: it distinguishes a particular person in the biblical record. The surrounding verse is needed to explain that person’s role or significance; the name itself does not provide that additional information.

word:hebrew:H2156.explanation: Zemorah means a pruned twig. It can also refer to a branch or vine branch.

word:hebrew:H231.explanation: This Hebrew word means “hyssop,” the name of a plant. It appears as an object used in several Old Testament commands and actions, including instructions recorded in Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers. The word occurs 10 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, showing a specific plant reference rather than a broad abstract idea. Its use in Scripture is connected with commanded acts and with imagery involving cleansing and restoration, while the precise force in any verse depends on that passage’s context.

word:hebrew:H2314.explanation: Chadar means to enclose, as a room. It can also refer to entering a private chamber.

word:hebrew:H2383.explanation: Hezion is a Hebrew name rendered “Hezion.” It functions as an identifying name, not as a general description, action, or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs once, at 1 Kings 15:18. The available scriptural connections place the name in relation to speech, giving, dwelling, and taking, but the surrounding verse text is not available here, so those connections do not establish a broader lexical meaning beyond the name itself.

word:hebrew:H2422.explanation: This Hebrew word is an adjective meaning “lively.” It describes a person or condition characterized by the quality of being lively, rather than naming an action, object, or place. In the Hebrew Bible, it occurs once, at Exodus 1:19, so its normal meaning is represented by this single occurrence. The precise force of the adjective in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text, which is not included here.

word:hebrew:H2596.explanation: Chanak means to dedicate or set something apart for a purpose.

word:hebrew:H2628.explanation: This Hebrew verb means “consume,” describing the action of using up or swallowing something. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Deuteronomy 28:38. As a verb, it expresses an action rather than a person, object, or quality. Its single occurrence means this word has a narrow recorded range in the Hebrew Bible, so its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage. The word is connected there with other terms describing what happens to the field and its produce.

word:hebrew:H2673.explanation: Chatsah means to cut or split in two, or to divide. It can describe dividing people into groups or dividing waters.

word:hebrew:H2808.explanation: Cheshbon means a contrivance or device; it can also mean reason or an account.

word:hebrew:H2853.explanation: This Hebrew word means “all.” It expresses the entirety of whatever it qualifies or describes, rather than a limited portion. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs twice, both in Ezekiel 16:4. The available record identifies it as a predicate, meaning it helps make an assertion about another word or element. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text, which is not included here.

word:hebrew:H2901.explanation: This Hebrew word means “spin.” It describes the action of turning or twisting fibers into thread or yarn. In the Old Testament, it appears twice, both times in Exodus 35, so its use is narrowly concentrated rather than broadly distributed across Scripture. It functions as an action word, focusing on the work being performed. Its precise role in each occurrence depends on the surrounding verse, but the central idea remains the act of spinning material.

word:hebrew:H3025.explanation: Yagor means to fear or be afraid.

word:hebrew:H3069.explanation: Yahweh means God. It is also used as God’s name in direct address, as when Abram speaks to him as Yahweh.

word:hebrew:H3087.explanation: Jehotsadak is the name of an Israelite, rendered Josedech in the KJV.

word:hebrew:H327.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “camels,” the animals named in two passages in Esther. It functions as a concrete noun, identifying the animals used in the royal dispatch described there. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Esther 8:10 and Esther 8:14. Its basic meaning is therefore straightforward: it identifies camels rather than an abstract idea, person, action, or quality. The surrounding verse text would be needed to explain the specific role these animals play in either passage.

word:hebrew:H3274.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, identifying an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Genesis 36, within genealogical material concerning birth and descent. Its role is connected with a person being named in a family line. The available material does not provide a separate definition or translation meaning for the name, so its safest ordinary sense is the individual’s name itself.

word:hebrew:H3340.explanation: This word refers to the Jezerites, a people group named in the Hebrew Old Testament. It functions as a group designation rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The word occurs only once in the Hebrew corpus, in Numbers 26:49, so its use is narrowly focused on identifying this group. The precise significance of the name in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the established meaning is simply “Jezerites.”

word:hebrew:H3421.explanation: Jorkeam is a personal name, not a general word describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 2:44, and the English rendering is “Jorkeam.” Its setting is a genealogy, where the name functions as an individual identified within a family line. No broader lexical sense is established for the name here.

word:hebrew:H352.explanation: Ayil means a ram, an animal used for offerings.

word:hebrew:H3524.explanation: Kabbîyr means vast or mighty. It can describe strength, as with a strong wind, or great age, as with very aged men. It can also describe having much.

word:hebrew:H3678.explanation: Kisse means a throne. It can also refer to a seat.

word:hebrew:H3717.explanation: Kaphal means to fold together. It can also describe making something double.

word:hebrew:H3762.explanation: Karmelitess means a female inhabitant of Carmel.

word:hebrew:H385.explanation: Ithamar is the name of one of Aaron’s sons.

word:hebrew:H3854.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “study,” describing that activity in its one recorded Old Testament occurrence. It appears in Ecclesiastes 12:12. Since the verse text and surrounding passage are not included here, its precise force in that sentence cannot be explained beyond this basic sense. The word therefore identifies study as the activity being referred to, without enough usage evidence to establish a wider range of meanings.

word:hebrew:H3898.explanation: Lacham means to battle or fight. It describes people fighting against opponents or a place in conflict.

word:hebrew:H3920.explanation: Lakad means to capture or occupy. It can also describe choosing someone by lot.

word:hebrew:H3986.explanation: This Hebrew verb means “refuse.” It describes a person or people unwilling to do what is requested or commanded. The word presents refusal as an expressed choice or response, rather than merely describing difficulty or inability. It appears four times in the Hebrew Old Testament, three times in Exodus and once in Jeremiah. Its precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage.

word:hebrew:H4024.explanation: Migdol is the name of a place in Egypt.

word:hebrew:H4121.explanation: Maharai is a personal name, rendered as “Maharai.” It identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. This name appears three times in the Hebrew Old Testament: once in 2 Samuel and twice in 1 Chronicles. The available passages preserve it consistently as “Maharai,” so its ordinary lexical function is simply to designate a person. The specific individual’s role or significance must be understood from the surrounding verse and passage.

word:hebrew:H4217.explanation: Mizrâch means sunrise or the east.

word:hebrew:H4262.explanation: Machmud means something desired, pleasant, or valuable.

word:hebrew:H4323.explanation: Mîykâl means a brook or streamlet.

word:hebrew:H4525.explanation: Masger can refer to a smith or to a prison.

word:hebrew:H4569.explanation: Maʻăbâr means a crossing-place, such as a ford or a pass.

word:hebrew:H4587.explanation: Meonothai is the name of an Israelite. Meonothai is named as the father of Ophrah.

word:hebrew:H4640.explanation: Maasai is an Israelite personal name.

word:hebrew:H477.explanation: Elisha is the name of a prophet.

word:hebrew:H4846.explanation: Merorah means bitterness or a bitter thing. It can also refer to gall or serpent venom.

word:hebrew:H4958.explanation: Masrêth means a pan, which is taken and used to pour something out.

word:hebrew:H499.explanation: Elazar is a personal name, rendered Eleazar in English.

word:hebrew:H4994.explanation: Na can express a plea, as in “I pray” or “beseech.” It can also mean “now” or “then,” depending on the sentence.

word:hebrew:H5081.explanation: Nadiv means willing or freely given. As a noun, it can refer to a noble or prince.

word:hebrew:H5100.explanation: Nehâmâh means snarling, and it can be rendered as roaring. It can also describe disquietness.

word:hebrew:H5247.explanation: Nimrah is a Hebrew proper name, used as the name of a place rather than as a general descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Numbers 32:3, and is rendered “Nimrah” in the available English renderings. Because it functions as a place-name, its meaning is primarily identification: it names a specific location. The surrounding verse and passage are needed to explain that location’s role in the account.

word:hebrew:H5311.explanation: Nephets means a storm as dispersing—scattering.

word:hebrew:H5441.explanation: This Hebrew word means a “thicket,” referring to a tangled mass of bushes or trees. It functions as a noun, naming dense vegetation rather than an action, person, or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Jeremiah 4:7. Because it appears only once and no verse text is provided here, its central lexical sense is clear, while the precise force of the word in that sentence belongs to its surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H550.explanation: Amnon is the name of a son of David.

word:hebrew:H5504.explanation: Sachar means profit from trade. It can also refer to merchandise.

word:hebrew:H5593.explanation: Saph is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Saph.” It identifies a named individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general concept. In the Hebrew Old Testament data here, it occurs once, at 2 Samuel 21:18, so its meaning is chiefly identifying rather than descriptive. The available rendering preserves it as a name, and no explicit definition is provided. Its precise role in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H5636.explanation: Sarpad means a nettle, a stinging plant, and is also rendered as a brier.

word:hebrew:H5690.explanation: This Hebrew word expresses love or describes something as lovely. It presents the idea of attractiveness or affection rather than an action, and its exact role depends on the sentence in which it appears. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, both times in Ezekiel 33. The word is rendered with the meaning "love" in one occurrence and "lovely" in the other, showing that it can express either the affection itself or the quality that draws affection.

word:hebrew:H5715.explanation: This Hebrew word means “testimony”—a witness, declaration, or enduring reminder that something has been stated or established. It commonly refers to the testimony associated with the covenant, including the tablets and the sacred chest that contained them. The word occurs 59 times in the Hebrew Bible, especially in Exodus, Psalms, and Numbers, and can function as something given, spoken about, guarded, or made. Its precise force in a particular verse depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H5759.explanation: Aviyl means a babe, young child, or little one.

word:hebrew:H5870.explanation: Ayin means an eye. It refers to eyes lifted toward heaven and to eyes pictured on a horn.

word:hebrew:H5935.explanation: This Hebrew word functions as a personal name, rendered “Alvan” or “Alian.” It identifies an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in genealogical passages at Genesis 36:23 and 1 Chronicles 1:40. Because no explicit definition is preserved, its meaning is best understood as the individual’s name, while the surrounding passage identifies the person being listed.

word:hebrew:H5979.explanation: Emdah means a station or place of standing.

word:hebrew:H5997.explanation: Amith means a companion, fellow, or kindred person. In these commands, it refers to another person who must be treated honestly and fairly.

word:hebrew:H6.explanation: Abad means to perish. It can also mean to destroy.

word:hebrew:H6031.explanation: Anah means to afflict or humble.

word:hebrew:H6127.explanation: This Hebrew word means “wrong.” It describes something as being morally or legally wrong rather than right. In its one Old Testament occurrence, it functions as a predicate—stating what something is or how it stands. The word appears in Habakkuk 1:4, and its precise force there is understood through the surrounding sentence and passage. Its connection with judgment and law reinforces its role in describing a condition recognized as wrong. word:hebrew:H6152.explanation: Arab means Arabia, a country east of Palestine.

word:hebrew:H6206.explanation: ʻÂrats means to dread or be terrified. It can also mean to harass. In another use, it describes oppressing someone.

word:hebrew:H6318.explanation: This Hebrew word is the personal name “Potiphar,” identifying a particular man rather than describing a general quality or action. It appears twice in the Old Testament Hebrew corpus, both times in Genesis: Genesis 37:36 and Genesis 39:1. The repeated rendering “Potiphar” indicates that the word functions as a proper name. Its exact significance in either verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic role is to identify this person.

word:hebrew:H6343.explanation: Pachad means sudden alarm or fear, and can also mean dread or terror.

word:hebrew:H64.explanation: This Hebrew word means “plain,” referring to a named or described place rather than an action or quality. It occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament, with both occurrences in Judges 11:33. The available wording supports the basic sense of a plain, while the precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage. It is therefore best understood as a place-related noun meaning “plain.”

word:hebrew:H644.explanation: This Hebrew verb means “bake,” describing the act of preparing food by cooking it in an oven or similar heated place. It can also appear in the rendered form “baked,” depending on how the sentence expresses the action. The word occurs 25 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, especially in passages involving bread, cakes, or other prepared food. Its ordinary sense is practical and direct: to cook something by heat until it is ready to eat.

word:hebrew:H6444.explanation: Peninnah is the name of an Israelite woman.

word:hebrew:H6488.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to something mentioned in Jeremiah 37:13, but its precise ordinary meaning cannot be determined from the available lexical information. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in that verse. The surrounding passage may clarify its role, yet the verse text and immediate context are not available here, so no more specific meaning should be assigned. Its recorded use is connected with speech and with other words in that verse, but those connections do not by themselves establish a translation.

word:hebrew:H6509.explanation: Parah means to bear fruit, literally or figuratively. It can describe being fruitful or growing.

word:hebrew:H6545.explanation: Peraʻ refers to hair on the head. It can also refer to locks of hair on the head.

word:hebrew:H6592.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “interpretation”: an explanation that makes the meaning of something understood. It refers to the act or result of making sense of a matter, rather than to the matter itself. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Ecclesiastes 8:1. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense is an interpretation or explanation that brings understanding to what is being considered.

word:hebrew:H6677.explanation: Tsavvar means the back of the neck, or simply the neck.

word:hebrew:H6699.explanation: Tsuwrah means a form, including the form or forms of a house.

word:hebrew:H6750.explanation: Tsâlal means to tingle, as ears do when they hear of evil.

word:hebrew:H6813.explanation: Tsaan describes moving something, including loading up beasts or migrating. It can also refer to being taken down, as with a tabernacle that is not taken down.

word:hebrew:H6848.explanation: Tsepha means a viper, also rendered as an adder or cockatrice.

word:hebrew:H688.explanation: Eqdach means a carbuncle or other fiery gem.

word:hebrew:H6884.explanation: Tsâraph means to fuse or refine, literally or figuratively. It can also describe testing, as when a word is tried.

word:hebrew:H7003.explanation: Kitron functions as a proper place name, identifying a specific location rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Judges 1:30, and is preserved in English as “Kitron.” Because no broader lexical definition is available, its ordinary meaning is the name of that location. The surrounding verse would be needed to explain the place’s particular role in that passage.

word:hebrew:H709.explanation: Argob is a proper name identifying a particular named entity in the Hebrew Scriptures. It is rendered “Argob” and functions as a name rather than as an ordinary descriptive word. The term appears five times in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, and 2 Kings. Its exact significance in any one verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic lexical role is to designate Argob by name.

word:hebrew:H7094.explanation: Qatsab means to cut or chop, including cutting something down. It can also describe something shorn.

word:hebrew:H7146.explanation: Qarachath means a bald spot on the back of the head. It can also refer figuratively to a bare or threadbare spot.

word:hebrew:H7212.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to beholding—looking at or observing something. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Ecclesiastes 5:11, so its ordinary meaning is supported by a single biblical use. As a noun-like expression connected with seeing, it points to the act or experience of looking rather than to a person or object itself. The exact force of the word in Ecclesiastes depends on the surrounding verse, but “beholding” clearly identifies its basic sense.

word:hebrew:H745.explanation: Arieh is a personal name, functioning as the designation of a person rather than as a description or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in 2 Kings 15:25, and the English rendering is “Arieh.” Its role is therefore to identify an individual in the passage. The surrounding verse is needed to explain that person’s specific actions or significance; the word itself primarily supplies the person’s name.

word:hebrew:H7454.explanation: Rea means a thought, an associated idea.

word:hebrew:H7498.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, referring to Rapha in the Old Testament genealogical records. It occurs twice, both times in 1 Chronicles 8, where it identifies a person within a family line. In one occurrence, the name is connected with a birth or begetting relationship, confirming its role as an individual’s name rather than a description of an action or quality. Its precise significance beyond the name itself is not stated by the available wording.

word:hebrew:H7520.explanation: Ratsad means to look askance—to look with envy or jealousy—and it can also describe leaping.

word:hebrew:H7586.explanation: Shaul is a personal name, rendered Saul in some English translations.

word:hebrew:H7616.explanation: Shabab means a fragment or ruin—something broken in pieces.

word:hebrew:H7739.explanation: Shᵉvâh means to resemble or be like. It can also describe making something like another thing.

word:hebrew:H792.explanation: “Eshbaal” is a personal name identifying an individual in Israel’s genealogical records. It is not presented here as a general action, quality, or object, but as the name of a person. The word occurs twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, both times in 1 Chronicles. Its recorded uses appear within genealogy material, where it is connected with family descent and birth relationships. The precise significance of the name itself is not stated in these occurrences, so its clear role is to identify this individual in the genealogy.

word:hebrew:H8028.explanation: Shelesh is a Hebrew personal name, rendered “Shelesh.” It functions as a name rather than a general description or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 7:35, and the available English renderings preserve it as “Shelesh.” Because this word occurs only in a genealogical reference and no verse text is provided here, its identity as a name is the clearest meaning that can be stated confidently.

word:hebrew:H8073.explanation: Shamlai is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing a general quality or action. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Ezra 2:46, and the English rendering preserves it as “Shamlai.” Because the available passage information does not provide a lexical definition or the name’s meaning, it is best understood simply as the name of the person listed there. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H8222.explanation: Sapham means the beard. It can also refer to the upper lip or lips.

word:hebrew:H8396.explanation: Tabor is the name of a mountain. It can also be the name of a city.

word:hebrew:H851.explanation: Eshtemoa is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H8514.explanation: Talʼûwbâh means desiccation, or great drought.

word:hebrew:H8583.explanation: Tou, also rendered Toi, is the name of a Syrian king.

word:hebrew:H907.explanation: Bad means a lie. It can also refer to a liar.
